accepted.reason: Best aligns with stated surveillance semantics (hospitalizations as lagged infection proxy) and matches the series’ current discovery patterns (SEIRS with delayed_I at 2–3 weeks). SEIR + delayed_I is parsimonious for 31 training points and avoids adding weakly identifiable compartments while still capturing a plausible admissions lag.

Observation-target alignment is good (hospitalizations plausibly lag infections), and SEIR is appropriately simple for a single-season series. A 1-week delay is plausible and provides a useful phase-sensitivity check versus 2 weeks without adding structural complexity.

SEIRS is consistent with the series’ discovered templates and keeps the recommended delayed_I observation mapping. However, waning immunity can be weakly identifiable in short single-season data; still acceptable as a controlled complexity increase given prior pattern support.

rejected.reason: SEIRS adds an extra dynamical degree of freedom (waning) while also using a 1-week delay that is less supported by the series’ current discovery patterns (2–3 weeks). With only 31 training points, this combination increases identifiability risk (waning vs transmission) without a strong semantic need.

Although H directly matches the hospitalization-rate target, an explicit hospitalization compartment is flagged as weakly identifiable for short single-season series. This proposal risks unstable inference of admission/duration/scaling parameters and may over-parameterize relative to the available data; delayed_I is more plausible here as a robust observation proxy.

suggested_edits.edit: Clarify that the 1-week delay is intended as a phase-robustness comparator to the 2-week baseline (not as the primary semantic assumption), given prior discovery favoring 2–3 weeks.

Add a note that waning-immunity effects may be weakly identified in a single season; consider constraining/regularizing the waning timescale conceptually (without adding new compartments) to reduce confounding with transmission.

If retained for completeness, explicitly frame as a low-priority sensitivity template due to identifiability risk in short series; avoid adding further hospitalization-process complexity beyond the single H state.
